what: Allegro MicroSystems designs sensor chips, principally magnetic ones. Its products detect position, speed and current without physical contact, and go mostly into cars — measuring wheel speed for braking systems, steering position, and current flow in electric vehicle battery and motor systems.
customers: Carmakers and their suppliers, who design the chips into specific vehicle platforms, plus industrial and data centre customers using current sensing in power systems.
money: Magnetic position and speed sensors and current sensors designed into vehicle platforms.
Sensors and power components for industrial automation, data centres and consumer products.
moat: Magnetic sensing is a specialised field where Allegro has decades of accumulated design knowledge, and a sensor designed into a vehicle platform stays there for the model’s production life — typically five to seven years — because requalifying a safety-related part mid-production is something carmakers do not do. Electric vehicles need substantially more of these chips than combustion ones.
risks: Revenue collapsed from $1.0B in 2024 to $725.0M in 2025 before recovering to $890.1M, which shows how sharply automotive inventory corrections hit chip suppliers.
Reported net income of $30.9M gives a price/earnings ratio of 189.5 and 37.4 times EV/EBITDA — the earnings are depressed and the multiples unusable.
Chinese carmakers increasingly source domestically, which threatens a meaningful share of future automotive semiconductor demand.
Fourteen analysts average a $48.21 target against a $28.42 price, a 70% gap reflecting disagreement about the recovery.
Automotive production volumes are outside the company’s control and have been weak.
opportunities: Electric vehicles use considerably more magnetic and current sensing than combustion vehicles, so content per vehicle rises as the fleet electrifies.
Design wins secure revenue for a vehicle platform’s entire production run, making future revenue visible once won.
Free cash flow of $104.4M on $1.0B of revenue, with debt of $305.9M against $168.8M of cash.
Decades of magnetic sensing expertise is a narrow but genuine technical position with few credible competitors.
Data centre power systems need current sensing, which is a new and growing market outside automotive.
watch: Content per vehicle and the design win pipeline. Vehicle production is the weather; content per vehicle is the growth, and the pipeline describes the next five years.
view: Allegro is a focused business — magnetic sensing, mostly for cars — and the focus is both its quality and its vulnerability. Measuring position, speed and current without physical contact is a specialised discipline built on decades of accumulated design knowledge, and there are few credible competitors. Once a sensor is designed into a vehicle platform it stays for the model’s entire production run, because no carmaker requalifies a safety-related component mid-production. That makes revenue visible for years once a design win is secured.

The electrification question runs the opposite way from the instinctive assumption, and this is the most important thing to understand about the company. An electric vehicle needs more of what Allegro sells, not less: current sensors throughout a high-voltage battery pack, position sensing in electric motors, monitoring across the power electronics. Content per vehicle rises as the fleet electrifies. Allegro is one of the auto semiconductor companies that benefits from the transition rather than being threatened by it.

What has gone wrong is an automotive inventory correction of unusual severity. Revenue fell from $1.0 billion to $725 million in a single year before recovering to $890 million — carmakers over-ordered chips after the shortage, then stopped ordering entirely while they worked through stock. That is a classic semiconductor cycle, it is not a judgement on the technology, and it has left reported net income at $31 million, which puts the price/earnings ratio at 189 and makes the multiples meaningless.

The genuine strategic risk is China. Chinese carmakers, who now produce an enormous share of global vehicles, are increasingly sourcing semiconductors domestically with explicit government encouragement. That is a structural loss of addressable market for every Western automotive chip supplier, and it is not cyclical. At $28.42 with fourteen analysts at $48.21, the market is pricing the cycle recovering and the China loss being manageable. Content per vehicle and design wins are the figures to follow; the income statement is currently describing an inventory correction, not a business.
bull: The inventory correction ends, electrification raises sensing content per vehicle, and data centre power sensing opens a new market outside automotive.
bear: Chinese carmakers source domestically and permanently shrink the addressable market, while automotive production stays weak against depressed earnings.
